I've struggled with sensitive and occasionally bleeding gums for years. No matter how diligently I thought I was brushing, my dental check-ups were always accompanied by a gentle, concerned lecture from my hygienist. During my last visit, my dentist strongly recommended two things: switching to an oscillating electric toothbrush and incorporating a water flosser into my routine. After some research, I invested in the Oral-B iO2 and, looking for a more budget-friendly option for the second item, I got the Hangsun Water Flosser. This combination has been nothing short of transformative. Let me start with the star of the show: the Oral-B iO2 Electric Toothbrush. From the first use, it felt like a professional cleaning. The iO Series is known for its unique round brush head and micro-vibrations, and the iO2 delivers this technology at a very accessible price point. The brushing sensation is incredibly thorough yet gentle. What truly amazes me is the result. Within just two weeks of consistent use, the bleeding has completely stopped. My gums look healthier, feel firmer, and are no longer tender. The built-in pressure sensor is a fantastic feature—it stops the pulsations and the smart ring light turns red if I press too hard, which was a bad habit of mine with a manual brush. The battery life is excellent. Now, for the Hangsun Water Flosser. I was a little skeptical at first, wondering if it was really necessary. Let me tell you, it absolutely is. While the Oral-B iO2 cleans the surfaces of my teeth and along the gumline impeccably, the Hangsun flosser tackles the spaces between my teeth and deep under the gums—areas a toothbrush simply can't reach.I fill it with warm water and use the lowest setting, and it effectively flushes out any leftover debris. It doesn't have the fancy features of some high-end brands, but it gets the job done reliably and efficiently. Together, they are the ultimate dream team for oral hygiene. The Oral-B iO2 provides the foundational clean, while the Hangsun Water Flosser performs the crucial finishing touches. Using them both morning and night has made my oral care routine feel complete and incredibly effective. My most recent dental appointment was a completely different story—no bleeding, no plaque buildup, and a lot of praise from my dentist, who was thrilled with the improvement in my gum health. If you're on the fence about either of these products, I cannot recommend them enough, especially as a pair. Investing in this duo is one of the best decisions I've made for my long-term health. My smile has never felt cleaner or healthier. Place the toothbrush head against your teeth at a 45-degree angle to the gum line. 3. Press the power button to start the toothbrush and move it gently across all tooth surfaces in a circular motion. 4. Brush the outer, inner, and chewing surfaces of all teeth for about 2 minutes, ensuring you spend equal time on each section. 5. Brush your tongue and the roof of your mouth to remove bacteria and freshen your breath. 6. Rinse your mouth and the toothbrush thoroughly after brushing. 7. Replace the toothbrush head every 3 months or when the bristles become frayed. For the £23 I bought it for I'd say this is definitely not the worst investment I've ever made, and it absolutely does give me a far better tooth clean than any manual brush ever could. From that perspective it absolutely does what I bought it for. That being said though, I think I have to echo a lot of what other people have been saying about it, from the point of view of its downsides. I havent had quite the egregious battery life other people seem to have been experiencing, but I'd also hesitate to call the battery life "good". I live by myself, and I manage to get anywhere from two to three days out of it before it needs charging again. Its not absolutely terrible and I bought it knowing the battery life was a weak point, but if you have a full family thats using it then the battery won't last very long at all. This is a problem, considering that there's no way to know when the battery is getting low other than just how strong the motor feels when you're using it. Looking at the instructions, it seems like other models have an LED on them, but this one doesnt even have a single one. This both means that its hard to get an exact idea of when the battery needs charging, and also means you wont know when exactly its done charging either (I think maybe some people are experiencing poor battery life because they arent leaving it on for long enough, precisely because of that). You sort of just have to guess at when it might be done or check how strong the motor feels. Dont get me wrong, I like that its simple and I dont think its inherently a bad product - I intend to keep it an use it even with its flaws, just because it does everything I need it to, only really cost the equivalent of a few packets of toothburshes, and having the integrated timer is really useful. However I feel like they made it a little too simple for its own good. Not having even a single LED on there does kind of harm the functionality, given that the battery life isnt exactly stellar to begin with. I'm ok with that on balance since I'm the only one using it here, but it may well be worth it to most people to move slightly further up the like to a slightly higer end brush. I feel like its also worth noting, while we're on the subject, that the brush's charger only has a shaver plug connector, and it doesnt include an adapter for a standard wall socket. Thats fine if you have a shaver plug, but I feel like to an extent those are a dying breed so most people will also need a shaver plug adapter to use a normal socket with it, which is worth noting since it adds to the cost and it isnt really mentioned on the product page (albeit not especially significantly). " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Great hydration and smooth skin, but beard wearers will need to get creative! The instructions for this hydrogel mask are incredibly clear, making the application process completely straightforward. On clean-shaven skin, like my girlfriend's face, the mask fits flawlessly with absolutely zero gaps. It hugs the contours of the face perfectly. Just keep in mind that this is a deep-treatment mask. It took about 3 to 4 hours to completely dry down, turn translucent, and absorb fully into the skin. The main challenge comes if you have a trimmed beard or facial hair. The hydrogel material cannot grip hair, so the lower half of the mask will not stick properly and tends to fall off. Only the upper section secured well to my forehead and upper cheeks.However, we found some great creative workarounds so nothing went to waste! My girlfriend applied the remaining jaw and chin section to my neck 😂, which worked beautifully. We also used the tiny punch-out eye and mouth patches creatively, placing the extra pieces above my eyebrows and using the mouth cutout across the bridge of my nose for targeted hydration. Pros:Truly delivers a noticeable boost in skin hydration and plumpness. Leaves the skin feeling incredibly smooth, refreshed, and deeply nourished. High-quality ingredients that genuinely work, offering great value for money. Cons: Not beard-friendly, as the lower half slides off facial hair. Requires 3–4 hours to dry, so it is best used when you have plenty of time or as an overnight mask. Final Verdict:If you have a smooth, clean-shaven face, this mask is an easy 5-star product because the fit and skin benefits are flawless. If you have a beard, the lower half simply won't stick. However, because it is highly effective and versatile enough to be repurposed on your neck and nose, it still deserves a solid 4 stars. Highly recommended, but beard wearers beware! For the last few years, my washing machine had been giving off the most horrendous smell after each wash, which I can only describe as an ungodly mix of sewage, garlic, and egg. It was absolutely disgusting, and the smell would spread throughout the house. I tried every solution I could think of, including bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, hot cycles, and even other chemical cleaners, but nothing worked. I cleaned every part of the machine, replaced the pipes, scrubbed the detergent drawer, cleaned the drip tray, and ran hot washes, but the smell just wouldn't go away. I was at my wit's end, especially with guests coming to stay, and I couldn’t bear the thought of them waking up to that awful odour. So, I scoured Amazon one last time and came across this Dr. Beckmann Service-it Deep Clean Washing Machine Cleaner. Its bold claims of removing 99.99% of bacteria, fungi, and viruses, as well as eliminating bad odours, seemed too good to be true, so I had to try it! All I can say is wow! Using it couldn’t be easier. Just empty the whole 250g box into the drum, no measuring required, and set your machine to run at a minimum of 60°C for at least an hour. I opted for a 90°C wash, which lasts for 2 hours on my machine, for extra thoroughness. After just one wash, the disgusting smell that had plagued my home for years was completely gone, and three weeks later, it still hasn’t returned. I’m absolutely amazed at how effective this product is. It left no mess, no residue, and it feels like I have a brand-new washing machine. For the price, it’s unbeatable. I paid £2.90 for the 250g pack, which is enough for one full clean, and I’ve seen the price drop lower. Given how effective it is, that’s an absolute bargain! I’ve already ordered a few more packs to use regularly, as it’s recommended to use every 1-2 months to keep your machine in top shape. The cleaner is supposed to leave a lemon fresh scent, though I didn’t really notice that. But honestly, the fact that my machine no longer smells at all is a win for me. Now all I can smell is my laundry detergent, and that’s good enough! I’ve tried a lot of other products, including well-known brands like Dettol, but none of them were able to tackle the odour like this. It also worked wonders on the limescale build-up in my 20-year-old machine, leaving the drum and seals sparkling clean. This cleaner is suitable for both front-loading and top-loading machines, and it’s great for prolonging the life of your appliance by preventing limescale and dirt build-up. If you’ve been dealing with an awful odour in your washing machine like I was, I can’t recommend this product enough. I wish I had found it sooner. It would have saved me so much frustration. I’ll definitely be using it regularly from now on, and I’m excited to try more from the Dr. Beckmann range. If you’re looking for a product that truly works and is great value for money, this is it! " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. You've seen this on Tiktok, that's why you're here, probably trying to ensure you buy a genuine Medicube product rather than risking a fake. Good call. I also saw this on Tiktok, and was baffled by the blatant lies and exaggerations, which I believe is the reason this product has 4 stars. Tiktok calls it.. well I won't say what Tiktok calls it in case it gets my review declined, but let's just say they compare it to filler. If you're buying this product because you believe it's got the same ingredients as implants(?), it's so powerful that if you put it on your finger it'll swell up like a balloon, or you will see instant results, then please believe me when I tell you that firstly - you are Tiktok's ideal demographic, and secondly - you're gonna be disappointed in this product. If you're buying it because you've read about volufiline, but maybe don't want to jump straight to stronger forms of it, like the Ordinary serum for example, and you're willing to give the skincare a chance to actually work, you might just love this product. It is not 'vaseline in a stick', nor is it some miracle product that's gonna immediately rid you of your eye bags and crows feet. It is a dose of hydration around areas that need a little more attention as we age, and the ingredients do have some scientific backing behind them - with the caveat that the effects are subtle and are not a replacement for filler. Volufiline stimulates fat cells, causing the plumping effect that's so grossly misrepresented on Tiktok. I've been using for about a week every day, and I am noticing subtle differences in my under eye area, the shadows are lessening, and the delicate skin feels hydrated. Skincare girlies (and guys) know that skincare products need 6 weeks to be tested properly, so I'm excited that I can visibly see improvements in such a short period. I like the application, the product being in stick form means I can easily apply it quickly without worrying about wasted product, which can be an issue with the Ordinary serum - although the comparison isn't fair as the products are completely different in strength. The product is very gentle, and I have eczema, sporadic psoriasis and sensitive skin in general, this has caused no redness, irritation or stinging. Value wise, the price is likely up due to the product going viral, but I was pleased with the results so in my opinion the product is worth it, I would also advise (but you know, who am I to tell you what to do?) to buy the genuine Medicube balm, rather than the crop of 'dupes' that have sprung up trying to cash in on the hype. You and your skin, particularly your eyes, deserve quality ingredients, not a mish mash of cheap imitations smushed together and marketed as a dupe. As I haven't tested the product for long enough to make a fair assessment on the long term effects, what I will say is that at worst, it's a convenient, quality dose of hydration for areas that need it most, and at it's best I can see improvements in glow, skin quality and volume in the areas of my face that need a little top up. Remember - if something seems too good to be true, it usually is. I like the product, I like Medicube in general as a brand, and I would recommend this product based on what I've seen so far. The formula is enriched with Botanical Glycerin to help nourish, soothe, and refresh. It is designed to cleanse while leaving skin soft and hydrated for up to 24 hours. Is the bottle made with recycled plastic, and is the formula vegan? Yes. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. ​I purchased the 6-pack of BRITA MAXTRA PRO Pure Performance Water Filter Cartridges, and I wanted to share my experience to help others who might be on the fence. Bottom line: great water filter, no issues, thank you! ​Size, Weight & Colour: These cartridges are standardized perfectly for BRITA jugs. They are compact (measuring about 5.7 x 10 x 7.6 cm) and very lightweight at just 0.11 kg each. They come in the standard white plastic casing. Because they are so small and light, storing the other five cartridges in the kitchen cupboard takes up virtually no space until you need them. ​Ease of Use: They are incredibly straightforward to swap out. If you've never used them before, it's virtually foolproof: just submerge the new filter in water to get the air bubbles out, push it firmly into the funnel of your jug until it clicks, and run a couple of cycles of water through it before drinking. ​Value for Money: Based on my experience and reading other reviews, the ongoing cost of replacing water filters every 4 weeks can add up. However, buying this 6-pack definitely softens the blow and provides excellent long-term value. You are set for roughly half a year! It’s also significantly cheaper than buying bottled water, and much better for the environment. ​Pros: ​Improved Taste: It noticeably removes chlorine, impurities, and limescale. Tap water tastes clean, and hot drinks (like tea or coffee) taste so much better without that nasty film on top. ​Bulk Value: The 6-pack is the most economical way to buy these, giving you months of supply in one go. ​Eco-friendly: A fantastic alternative to single-use plastic water bottles, and BRITA has a great recycling scheme for the used cartridges. ​Cons: ​Ongoing Expense: The only real downside is that you do have to replace them monthly for the best performance, which is an ongoing running cost. ​Answering common buyer questions: ​Does it really help with hard water? Yes. If you live in a hard water area, you will immediately notice a reduction in limescale build-up in your kettle. ​Are they compatible with older jugs? Yes, they fit perfectly into standard BRITA jugs (like the Marella or Aluna) just like previous standard Maxtra versions did. ​Overall, I highly recommend this 6-pack. Next set of slides Important information Safety Information: Keep out of the reach and sight of children. Do not use this product… - if you have ever had a bad reaction to any of the ingredients. If this applies to you, get advice from a doctor or pharmacist without using Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo. If you are pregnant or breast-feeding - you can use Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo if you are pregnant, think you might be pregnant or are breast-feeding. Special warnings about this product - this medicine contains 24% w/w sodium laurilsulfate in each application. Sodium laurilsulfate may cause local skin reactions (such as stinging or burning sensation) or increase skin reactions caused by other products when applied on the same area. - as with most shampoos, if any gets into your eyes bathe them gently with water. - if you have been regularly using a lotion or cream, which contains a steroid (such as betamethasone or hydrocortisone) to control your dandruff, gradually use it less over 2 - 3 weeks as you start to use Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo. This will stop your condition flaring up while Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo starts to work. If you have any questions about stopping your steroid lotion or cream, speak to your doctor or pharmacist. If anyone accidentally swallows this product if anyone accidentally swallows Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo, contact a doctor or your nearest accident & emergency department (casualty) taking this leaflet and pack with you. Possible side-effects Nizoral anti-dandruff shampoo can have side-effects like all medicines, although these don't affect everyone and are usually mild. If you experience any of the following, stop using the medicine and talk to your doctor: - severe allergic reactions including swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat uncommon side-effects (less than 1 in 100 people) which may occur include: - application site reactions including itching, irritation, blistering, red, dry or tender skin or a skin burning sensation - inflamed hair follicles, hair loss or changes in hair texture - increased tear production - skin rash and dry skin rare side-effects (less than 1 in 1000 people) which may occur include: - a change in the way some things taste - eye irritation - acne - skin inflammation (dermatitis) - flaking skin - application site reactions including blistering and over-sensitivity (allergic) reactions - general allergic reaction (over sensitivity) other side effects which occur but it is unknown how often: - hair discolouration and hives, which is known as nettle rash or urticaria reporting of side-effects if you get any side-effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse. Superior, natural-looking colour with a blend of 3 tones and highlights, plus soft and shiny hair, thanks to conditioners in the formula and in the kit. How long will the effects of Nice'n Easy last? You can enjoy long-lasting colour and shine for up to 8 weeks. Should I apply Nice'n Easy to dry or damp hair? Apply to dry hair that's free of styling product build up. Blocked nose, head cold, congestion, headache, fever, aches, and pain. How to relive symptoms of a cold? You can help relieve a blocked nose with Sudafed decongestant spray or tablets. You can ease aches and pains with painkillers like Paracetamol, or Ibuprofen. Sudafed capsule products contain paracetamol and a decongestant. How long does a cold last? It can vary, but you should begin to feel better in about a week or two. See your GP if your symptoms don't improve after 10 days. What is Sinusitis? A condition in which the cavities around the nasal passages become inflamed and swollen. Acute sinusitis can be triggered by a cold or allergies and may resolve on its own. What causes a blocked nose? A blocked nose occurs when the nose lining becomes inflamed and swollen. This causes the nasal passages to become narrower and therefore more easily blocked up. The FA6813’s electrochemical sensing technology enables a fast reaction to rising levels of carbon monoxide (CO), aka ‘The Silent Killer’, helping to keep you and your family safe. LOUD ALARM: If dangerous levels of CO are detected in your home, the carbon monoxide detector will alert you with 4 loud chirps—85 dB(A) at 3 m (min)—and a flashing red ‘CO’ LED light. TEST BUTTON: Press the large test button to ensure your CO detector is working properly. A loud, high-pitched sound and the red LED flashing four times will verify that the alarm is functioning correctly. Test your device regularly (we recommend once a week). LOW BATTERY ALERT: A flashing amber '!' and an audible chirp will alert you when the batteries need replacing. SLEEP EASY FUNCTION: If the low battery alert sounds overnight and you are unable to immediately replace the batteries, press the large test button to silence the low battery alert. This activates the Sleep Easy mode on the carbon monoxide monitor, muting the low battery chirp for 8 hours while the amber light flashes. Replace the batteries ASAP. CRESCENDO TEST: This feature helps to protect your hearing by allowing you to choose the volume level of the test alarm. ALARM MEMORY: With the alarm memory function, a red LED will flash to let you know with a visual indication that there has been a previous CO alarm activation within the last 30 days. Ventilate and call a technician. REPLACEABLE BATTERIES: Each device is fitted with 1 year replaceable batteries. In the event of the CO alarm sounding, follow these 3 steps: VENTILATE : Keep calm; open doors and windows to ventilate your home. Stop using fuel-burning appliances and turn them off. EVACUATE : Evacuate the property immediately. RING FOR HELP: If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. Do not use appliances until they have been checked by an expert. Get medical help for anyone suffering the effects of CO poisoning. What are the symptoms of CO poisoning? Symptoms of CO poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, seizures, chest pain, disorientation, and loss of consciousness. Who should I call in the event of a CO leak? If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. What are the sources of CO? The common sources of Carbon Monoxide (CO) are cookers, fires, boilers, oil and gas boilers, portable generators, oil or solid fuel cookers, gas or paraffin heaters, barbecues (BBQs), clogged chimneys, wood or gas fireplaces, cigarette smoke or any fossil fuel‑burning appliances. This means someone could potentially have repeated intermittent exposure to toxic amounts of carbon monoxide without carbon monoxide alarms necessarily activating. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. Dopo aver provato praticamente tutti i detergenti CeraVe, posso dire che questa è la versione che preferisco in assoluto per la mia pelle. Ho una pelle mista, quindi con alcune zone che tendono a lucidarsi e diventare più oleose e altre che invece possono risultare più secche. Per questo ho sempre cercato un detergente che riuscisse a pulire bene senza lasciarmi quella sensazione di pelle "tirata" dopo il lavaggio. Nel corso del tempo ho provato praticamente tutte le versioni della linea CeraVe. Ho iniziato anche dall'olio detergente, proprio perché cercavo qualcosa di estremamente delicato. Mi è piaciuto, soprattutto per la sensazione che lasciava e per la profumazione, ma personalmente non era quello con cui mi trovavo meglio. Ho poi provato la crema detergente e, invece, non sono riuscito ad apprezzarla particolarmente. Soprattutto in estate, la sensazione durante l'utilizzo mi risultava troppo simile a quella di spalmare una crema sul viso e non era la tipologia di detersione che cercavo. Con la Schiuma Detergente, invece, ho trovato finalmente il compromesso che cercavo. LA SCHIUMA FA DAVVERO LA DIFFERENZA La prima cosa che si nota è ovviamente la consistenza: a contatto con l'acqua il detergente produce una bella schiuma. Ora, dal punto di vista scientifico, più schiuma non significa necessariamente più pulizia. È un aspetto importante perché spesso associamo inconsciamente una grande quantità di schiuma a un prodotto più efficace. Però c'è anche un aspetto più pratico e personale: a me la schiuma piace. Durante la skincare trovo molto più piacevole massaggiare una schiuma sul viso rispetto a una crema o a un olio. È una piccola cosa, ma secondo me il fatto che una routine sia piacevole da fare aumenta anche la probabilità di riuscire a mantenerla con costanza. La skincare, alla fine, non è soltanto una questione di ingredienti: anche la sensorialità del prodotto conta nell'esperienza quotidiana. PERCHÉ È ADATTA ALLA PELLE MISTA La formula è pensata per detergere rimuovendo sebo, impurità e residui senza compromettere eccessivamente la barriera cutanea. CeraVe utilizza in questa linea ceramidi e acido ialuronico, ingredienti interessanti soprattutto perché la detersione non dovrebbe limitarsi a "sgrassare" la pelle, ma dovrebbe cercare di mantenere un buon equilibrio tra pulizia e comfort. Le ceramidi, in particolare, sono lipidi naturalmente presenti nella barriera cutanea e svolgono un ruolo importante nel mantenimento della funzione barriera. È quindi sensato trovarle all'interno di una linea cosmetica che punta a detergere senza lasciare la pelle inutilmente impoverita. Il detergente contiene inoltre niacinamide, ingrediente molto versatile che viene utilizzato frequentemente nelle formulazioni destinate alle pelli miste o impure. Una cosa che apprezzo è proprio il fatto che, dopo il risciacquo, non mi rimane quella sensazione di "pelle che tira" che personalmente associo a una detersione troppo aggressiva. COME LO UTILIZZO Ne basta davvero poco. Inumidisco il viso, erogo una piccola quantità di prodotto e lo massaggio delicatamente sulla pelle, senza sfregare eccessivamente. Poi risciacquo con acqua. Non vedo la necessità di utilizzare una quantità enorme di detergente: la schiuma si distribuisce bene e una confezione da 473 ml dura davvero a lungo. Ed è proprio questo uno dei motivi per cui considero questo formato particolarmente conveniente. 473 ML: UN FORMATO CHE FA LA DIFFERENZA Questa secondo me è una delle caratteristiche più sottovalutate. Molti detergenti che mi incuriosiscono, soprattutto alcuni prodotti coreani, vengono venduti in confezioni da 150, 200 o 250 ml. Non è necessariamente un problema, ma quando si utilizza un detergente ogni giorno, mattina e/o sera, il prodotto finisce abbastanza rapidamente. Qui invece abbiamo 473 ml, quindi quasi mezzo litro. Considerando che ne basta poco ad ogni utilizzo, una confezione mi dura veramente parecchio. Per una skincare quotidiana è un vantaggio enorme, soprattutto se si vuole evitare di ricomprare continuamente il detergente. LA MIA ESPERIENZA Dopo aver provato praticamente tutta la gamma detergente CeraVe, questa è quella che ricomprerei più volentieri. Non perché sia necessariamente "la migliore" per qualsiasi tipo di pelle, ma perché è quella che si adatta meglio alle mie esigenze. La mia pelle mista ha bisogno di una detersione che mi faccia sentire il viso pulito senza trasformare il lavaggio in un momento in cui la pelle viene aggredita. La schiuma rende inoltre l'utilizzo molto piacevole e il formato da 473 ml permette di utilizzarlo quotidianamente senza preoccuparsi troppo dei consumi. " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Comfortable, True-to-Size Gloves That Don't Tear Easily I've tried quite a few disposable gloves over the years for various jobs, including DIY, maintenance work, and more 3D resin printing, and these have impressed me more than expected. Sizing is often an issue with disposable gloves, as many of the cheaper ones I've bought in the past tend to come up smaller than advertised. An XL can sometimes fit more like a Large. Thankfully, these are true to size. The XL fits me perfectly, with no tight spots and no excess material at the fingertips, making them comfortable to wear while still allowing good dexterity. The gloves strike a nice balance in thickness. They're not the thickest nitrile gloves I've used, but they're certainly not flimsy or paper-thin either. They provide a reassuring level of protection while still allowing enough finger sensitivity for detailed tasks. One thing I particularly like is how much stretch they have. They slide on easily and stretch well without immediately tearing, which is something I've experienced with cheaper gloves in the past. My main use for these has been 3D resin printing, where reliable hand protection is essential. During several printing sessions, I had no issues with resin penetrating the gloves, and they held up well while handling resin-coated parts. They gave me confidence that my hands were properly protected throughout the process. Being powder-free and latex-free is another plus, especially for anyone with latex sensitivities or who simply prefers gloves that don't leave residue behind. They're comfortable enough to wear for extended periods and don't have an overpowering chemical smell when first opened. Considering the fit, durability, comfort, and level of protection they provide, I think these offer excellent value for money. They perform exactly as I'd hoped and compare favourably with gloves that cost considerably more. Once this box is finished, I'll happily buy another.
